sections.body_md: You usually build trust through steady one-on-one conversations, reflection, and protected space. You tend to value people who are reliable, concrete, and consistent in day-to-day follow-through. In conflict you often default to harmony and emotional tone, so it helps to make your principles explicit. In close relationships and teamwork, you usually prefer flexibility, openness, and room to adapt.

sections.body_md: ISFP-A and ISFP-T share the same ISFP core. Within taste, experience and quiet personal expression, the useful difference is how the two A/T styles handle confidence, pressure, feedback and self-correction, not which one is better.

content.quick_answer: ISFP-A and ISFP-T share the same ISFP core. Within taste, experience and quiet personal expression, the useful difference is how the two A/T styles handle confidence, pressure, feedback and self-correction, not which one is better.

faq.answer: Around taste, experience and quiet personal expression, the main difference is usually confidence style, stress response, feedback processing and self-correction, not a change in the ISFP core.
faq.question: What is the main ISFP-A vs ISFP-T difference?
faq.reason: Covers comparison intent and claim boundary.

faq.answer: No. A/T describes style differences, not a ranking. ISFP situations can reward steadiness, caution or revision in different ways.
faq.question: Is ISFP-A better than ISFP-T?
faq.reason: Covers comparison intent and claim boundary.

faq.answer: Look at your response to taste, experience and quiet personal expression-related pressure, criticism, uncertainty and post-decision review rather than treating the label as a verdict.
faq.question: How can I tell whether I am ISFP-A or ISFP-T?
faq.reason: Covers comparison intent and claim boundary.

faq.answer: No. It can support ISFP work-style reflection, but it should not replace skills, experience, values or context.

faq.reason: Covers comparison intent and claim boundary.
